findings.title: The sync path returns a Fetch Response instead of the provider's token response
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, while the fallback returns each provider's native response shape. Callers are written for those native shapes: Google reads `res.data`, Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads token fields directly. Those accesses fail or produce undefined token fields in sync mode, so refreshes break for these integrations. Normalize the sync response to the shape each caller expects, or update callers to parse the response consistently.

findings.title: The minimum schema strips refreshed token fields
findings.body: This computed key is a literal property name, not a wildcard for numeric expiry fields. Zod objects also strip unrecognized keys by default, so parsing a synced response retains only `access_token` and discards expiry and other provider fields. Callers then persist incomplete credentials; for example, Zoom assigns the missing `refresh_token` from the parsed response and can no longer refresh again, while Office 365 does not receive a new expiry. Preserve the response fields and explicitly extract the expiry value.

findings.title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses credential syncing
findings.body: This refresh request still calls Salesforce directly rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. With credential syncing configured, Salesforce credentials therefore continue to refresh against Cal.com's app credentials instead of the self-hosted source of truth, so the feature does not work for Salesforce.

findings.title: Salesforce client is initialized with the pre-refresh access token
findings.body: The refresh response is saved to the credential, but the connection below is constructed using `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token loaded before the refresh. When that token has expired, the current operation still uses the expired token and fails even though a new token was successfully obtained. Initialize the connection with `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
findings.body: The third argument is used by `refreshOAuthTokens` as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, which is the credential row's database ID. A sync endpoint that looks up credentials by Cal.com user ID will look up the wrong user and cannot refresh this credential. Pass the owning user's ID instead.
